FIP.thesis_summary: A signed $1.52 billion sale of the Long Ridge power plant to MARA, awaiting only a change-of-control approval from the energy regulator, guided to close by the end of the third quarter of 2026 and cutting total debt from $3.8 billion to $2.4 billion; the shares at $4.23 sit near their fifty-two-week low against a $9.00 event-resolved value and a realistic $2.75 deal-break price.
FIP.dated_milestone: Change-of-control approval from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, application filed 8 May 2026 in docket EC26-92, guided by management to arrive in the middle of the third quarter of 2026, with the sale closing by 30 September 2026 on the seller's guidance. Nearest scheduled checkpoint: second-quarter 2026 results after the close on Wednesday 5 August 2026, with the conference call at 8:00 a.m. Eastern on Thursday 6 August 2026.
FIP.kill_risk: [CONFIRMED_WITH_CORRECTIONS] The '14x private-market mark' that anchors the entire sum-of-the-parts is not what the buyer says it paid. The bull derives 14x by annualising Long Ridge's outage-impacted Q1-2026 adjusted EBITDA of $26.4m ($105.6m) against the $1.512bn base price. MARA's own 30 April 2026 announcement states Long Ridge contributes approximately $144 million of annualised adjusted EBITDA (second-half 2025 basis, reflecting the February 2025 hedge swaps and the June 2025 capacity payments) - i.e. the buyer underwrote roughly 10.5x, not 14x. FIP.dossier_note: Buy it now, and size it as a levered stub with a live event rather than as an arbitrage with a floor. The event is genuine. A definitive agreement was signed on 29 April 2026 to sell the Long Ridge power plant to MARA for about $1.52 billion, the regulatory application was filed on 8 May in docket EC26-92, the buyer cleared its bondholder consents in June, no financing contingency exists, and management has guided to approval by the middle of the third quarter. Nothing about it has fired, and the shares have actually fallen since the announcement, so none of the re-rating has been spent. At $4.23, close to the fifty-two-week low of $3.90 and against a high of $7.94, you are being paid to wait for a transaction that reduces total debt from $3.8 billion to $2.4 billion and saves about $30 million of interest a year, on a company whose surviving railroads grew earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation 31% year over year. There is no wash-out worth waiting for; this is the wash-out. Two things keep this from being the maximum-conviction version of this setup. The first is the floor. The entry carried into this review assumes $3.90 of downside protection, and that number is a chart level, not a recovery value. Book equity is negative $303.1 million, there is no net cash, operating cash flow was negative $69.4 million last quarter, and the filing's own liquidity assurance is expressly conditioned on this sale closing. A deal-break realistically prices the shares

VRDN.thesis_summary: The catalyst has already fired: the FDA approved Lumvoa (veligrotug-vvze) for thyroid eye disease on 26 June 2026, four days ahead of its 30 June target date and with a broader label than expected - and the stock is at $19.70 a month later, so the re-rating we were waiting to be paid for has been spent without paying, leaving roughly 52% upside to a $30 good-launch value against 57% downside to an $8.50 cash-based floor.
VRDN.dated_milestone: FDA approval granted 26 June 2026 (the target decision date was 30 June 2026) - fired, favourably and early, with the launch beginning the same week. Remaining calendar, none of it hard or binding: second-quarter results expected around 5 August 2026 (a stub month of launch revenue); management's guidance of broad insurance coverage within six to nine months of launch, pointing to roughly December 2026 through March 2027; a company-controlled approval filing for elegrobart targeted for the first quarter of 2027; and a European decision expected during 2027 on the application accepted in February 2026.
VRDN.kill_risk: [REFUTED] The catalyst has fired and nothing dated, binding or agency-controlled replaces it. Verified against the company's own 26 June 2026 release: the FDA approved Lumvoa (veligrotug-vvze) 'for the treatment of thyroid eye disease regardless of thyroid eye disease activity or duration', four days ahead of the 30 June 2026 PDUFA target action date, with no advisory committee, no complete response letter, and immediate launch -- physicians 'can prescribe Lumvoa tomorrow'. That is the best available version of the event this sleeve underwrote, and the tape refused it: the live quote is $19.70

VRDN.dossier_note:
This is a pass for now, and the reason is simple enough to state in one sentence: we were underwriting a dated regulatory decision, that decision arrived on 26 June 2026 - early, clean, and with a broader label than we expected - and the stock is at $19.70 a month later. When the best available outcome of a binary event does not pay, the market is pricing something the event did not address, and continuing to hold is no longer the trade we sized. It is a different trade wearing the old trade's clothes.

What the market is pricing is the 30 March 2026 data on elegrobart, the under-the-skin follow-on. That trial met its goal but at roughly 36 to 45 placebo-adjusted percentage points against about 64 for the approved infused drug, and the shares fell roughly a third that day and never recovered. The self-administered format is what was supposed to carry a chronic-disease franchise over a decade. A weaker version of it is a smaller company, and an approval for the infused drug does not repair that.

Two corrections to our own file, pulling in opposite directions. First, the balance sheet is much stronger than we carried: the company raised $350 million gross in May 2026 - shares at $17.00 plus 1.75% notes due 2032 - and collected a $75 million approval milestone from its royalty partner in late June, so cash is roughly $1.0 billion, not $600 million. EYPT.thesis_summary: Phase 3 LUGANO topline for DURAVYU in wet age-related macular degeneration - live, unfired, fully enrolled with the 56-week endpoint window already passed, expected August 2026 (the 31 July board date does not verify; the quarterly earnings date is estimated nearer 4 August) - offering +208% to a $37.50 win against -67% to a $4.00 failure floor, with the mechanism independently de-risked by a same-class Phase 3 success on 17 February 2026 and 26.4% of the float sold short.
EYPT.dated_milestone: Topline Phase 3 LUGANO data for DURAVYU (vorolanib intravitreal insert) in wet age-related macular degeneration, expected August 2026, with the confirmatory LUCIA trial reading roughly two months later. Management guided 'beginning mid-year' on the 6 May 2026 first-quarter call; current expectations place LUGANO in August 2026. CORRECTION: the watch-board hard date of 31 July 2026 is not corroborated by any company disclosure - no scheduled release, no regulatory clock, and the second-quarter earnings date is independently estimated nearer 4 August 2026. The event is nonetheless mechanically forced: LUGANO enrolled over 400 patients and closed enrolment in May 2025 with a 56-week primary endpoint, so last-patient-last-visit has passed and the data exist. Supporting dated evidence: third consecutive clean independent Data Safety Monitoring Committee review announced 14 May 2026; as of 2 May 2026 all active treatment-arm patients had reached the week 32 second-dose visit and over 35% had taken a third dose at week 56. Secondary dated items: diabetic macular edema trials COMO and CAPRI guided to complete enrolment in the third quarter of 2026; federal DEXYCU settlement executed 17 July 2026 with a five-year Corporate Integrity Agreement effective 13 July 2026.

EYPT.dossier_note:
Buy it now, and size it for a full loss. This is the setup this funnel exists to find, with one honest defect that keeps it from the top score. 

Start with what verifies. The catalyst is live and unfired: as of 27 July 2026 the most recent company news is an executive appointment on 13 July and an inducement-grant filing on 16 July. No topline exists. The event is weeks away and it is self-enforcing - LUGANO closed enrolment in May 2025 and reads at 56 weeks, so the last patient's final visit has passed and the data are being cleaned now. The company is financed straight through it, with $223 million at 31 March 2026 and runway into the fourth quarter of 2027, no debt in the way, and no offering on file. Safety has been cleared three consecutive times by the independent monitoring panel, most recently on 14 May 2026. Management has hit its process commitments - enrolment ran ahead of plan, disclosure has been granular to the level of individual dosing visits - and is spending real money on a commercial organisation ahead of a result. 

The finding that decides the name is external. On 17 February 2026 a competitor proved, at Phase 3, that a slow-release tyrosine kinase inhibitor implant maintains vision in wet age-related macular degeneration: 74.1% versus 55.8% at week 36, a 21.1 point gap sustained at week 52, with clean safety. LZM.dated_milestone: One real calendar item and one real deadline, neither of which is the catalyst itself. (1) First-half 2026 interim financial results on 29 July 2026, with an investor webcast at 10:00 a.m. New York time hosted by chief executive Chris Showalter and chief financial officer Ingo Hofmaier -- confirmed by the company on 27 July 2026 and verified today. This is a disclosure venue at which management must either produce the concluded process or explain a second missed milestone; it resolves nothing by itself. (2) The Taurus senior secured bridge matures on 31 July 2027, which is the outer bound on how long this can drift -- a deadline that works for the lender, not the shareholder. The catalyst proper -- the strategic-partner transaction -- has no announced date, and the two gates behind it, the Framework Agreement amendment with the Tanzanian government and the power supply agreements, are undated as well.

LZM.dossier_note:
This is a real event on a broken clock, and the discipline that makes this funnel work is the discipline to say so.

Start with what is true. Kabanga is a genuine tier-one orebody -- among the largest and highest-grade development-ready nickel sulfide deposits anywhere, in the cheapest quarter of the cost curve, with an independently prepared study value of $1.58 billion against a $298 million company. The sale process is real, competitive and advanced, corroborated by a wire-service leak specific enough that the company had to respond on 8 June 2026. If it concludes at a defensible fraction of study value, $7.00 is a defensible number and this roughly doubles.

Now what is not true. This is not a defined-risk event position, and treating it as one is the error the catalyst discipline exists to prevent. There is no date: the guided mid-2026 build decision lapsed silently, and 'concluding shortly' was said eighty-nine days ago. There is nothing binding: no agreement, no outside date, no regulator on a clock, no contractual payout. Two hard prerequisites -- a sovereign fiscal amendment and a utility power agreement -- are themselves undated, and one of them cannot be scheduled by anybody. And the floor our board carried at $2.60 is folklore. DDL.thesis_summary: Signed SPA (5 Feb 2026): Meituan subsidiary Two Hearts Investments buys Dingdong's China business for US$717M cash; with the pre-closing draw right (up to US$280M before 31 Aug 2026) total cash proceeds run up to US$997M, ~ $4.60/ADS gross vs $2.48 traded. Shareholders approved 27 Mar 2026; the company INTENDS (board absolute discretion, not binding) to return >=90% of post-closing cash via buybacks/dividends. Gating condition is SAMR anti-monopoly clearance (undated by regime design); contractual long-stop ~5 Feb 2027 (12 months from signing, extendable by mutual consent). Verified UNFIRED as of 4 Aug 2026: no clearance, no closing, no company communication since 21 May 2026, no SEC filing since 26 May 2026. Near-term observable: Q2 results (~20 Aug 2026 per aggregators, undated by company) will show whether the <=$280M draw was exercised before the 31 Aug soft date. Buyer break fees US$150M/US$75M tiered; company fee US$75M.
DDL.kill_risk: The single most load-bearing claim - that closing cash actually reaches shareholders - does not fully survive: the 27 Mar 2026 AGM resolution is EMPOWERING, not binding (board may deploy cash 'in its absolute discretion'), the 10 Feb release carries express no-assurance language, and the company is founder-controlled with super-voting shares. If the deal closes but the board returns only ~half the cash, value is ~ $2.41/ADS - BELOW the $2.48 tape; the position is a governance bet stacked on a regulatory bet. Secondary: SAMR clearance is undated and could run past the (extendable) Feb 2027 long-stop; passing 31 Aug 2026 without the draw is not disprovable evidence of trouble but would remove the near-term confirm.

THRM.dossier_note:
Pass for now. The reason is not that the business is bad or the deal is broken. Both are in reasonable shape. The reason is that we are being asked to buy an event that has already happened, at a price that reflects it.

Our board holds Gentherm as a merger arbitrage gated on United States antitrust risk. That description does not survive contact with the record. The antitrust waiting period was terminated early on 26 March 2026, four months ago, and international clearance is also in hand. Nor was this ever an arbitrage: Gentherm is the acquirer in a Reverse Morris Trust, issuing about 20.7 million of its own shares to absorb Modine's Performance Technologies business. Its shareholders receive no fixed consideration, no exchange ratio protection and no break fee. There is no contractual price to converge to, which means there is no spread and never was one.

The arithmetic is decisive. Our entry's recorded reward-to-risk of 2.87 implies a cost basis near $33.60. The shares closed at $42.07 on 27 July 2026 after a 12.4% jump on strong second-quarter results. Against a $44 target and a $30 floor, that is about 5% of upside against about 29% of downside, a ratio near 0.16 to 1. Reconciling the favourable case of roughly $52 per share against the adverse case of roughly $30 gives a probability-weighted value of about $43 per share, which is 2.7% above the current price. ZYME.thesis_summary: Zymeworks holds the economics on zanidatamab (Ziihera), which partner Jazz Pharmaceuticals has under FDA Priority Review for first-line HER2-positive locally advanced/metastatic gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma, PDUFA target action date 2026-08-25. U.S. approval triggers a $250M milestone payment from Jazz to Zymeworks (roughly $3.40 per share on ~73.6M shares) plus tiered royalties on a first-line indication far larger than the already-approved second-line biliary setting. The event is dated, binding, idiosyncratic, and unfired: Jazz's own 2Q26 release of 2026-08-03 says it is "prepared to launch Ziihera in HER2+ 1L GEA immediately following FDA approval," i.e. the partner reconfirmed the August window one day before this review. The application carries Priority Review, Breakthrough Therapy Designation and Real-Time Oncology Review on a positive Phase 3 (HERIZON-GEA-01: median OS 26.4 vs 19.2 months, PFS 12.4 vs 8.1 months vs trastuzumab/chemo), which supports a high approval probability (~85%). The live anomaly is price, not process: shares have fallen from $27.07 on 2026-07-09 to $21.81 on 2026-08-03 (-19%) with no adverse disclosure found in filings, press releases or news.
ZYME.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim is the $27 win leg, and it is the weakest link - not the approval odds. At the live $21.81 with my $17 lose leg, a $27 win leg implies the market is pricing only ~48% odds of approval ((21.81-17)/(27-17)), which is implausible for a Priority Review / Breakthrough / RTOR sBLA on a positive Phase 3 whose partner is staging a launch. The more likely reconciliation is that the market's win-leg value is ~$22-23, not $27: the $250M milestone is largely pre-committed (roughly $219M of closing cash for the Theravance acquisition plus an authorised $125M buyback, against ~$46-50M a quarter of operating burn), Zymeworks keeps only 70% of Ziihera royalties after the March 2026 Royalty Pharma note, and first-line royalty cash is years out. If so, the trade can be right on the event and flat on the stock - approval fires, the milestone lands, and the shares do not re-rate. The four-week, no-news drift from $27.07 to $21.81 into a dated binary is consistent with that reading, and is the honest residual risk.

ZYME.dossier_note:
CATALYST VERIFIED LIVE AND UNFIRED (as of 2026-08-04). Jazz/Zymeworks zanidatamab (Ziihera) sBLA in 1L HER2+ unresectable locally advanced or metastatic gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma, PDUFA target action date 2026-08-25, Priority Review + Breakthrough Therapy Designation + Real-Time Oncology Review, on HERIZON-GEA-01 (n=914; median OS 26.4 mo for zanidatamab/tislelizumab/chemo vs 19.2 mo for trastuzumab/chemo, ~28% reduction in risk of death; median PFS 12.4 vs 8.1 mo). No approval, CRL, advisory committee or timeline change has been announced. RTOR means the risk skews EARLY, not late - the decision can land before 2026-08-25, so treat the milestone as an outer bound.

VALUATION AXES (binary_prob), shares ~73.6M (mktcap $1,604.6M / $21.81):
- Win leg $27. Components: (a) $250M Jazz milestone on U.S. approval = $3.40/share of cash, unencumbered by the Royalty Pharma note (that note is serviced only by 30% of royalties, capped at 1.65x by 2033 / 1.925x after; Zymeworks retains 70% and full rights revert on repayment); (b) de-risking of the first-line royalty stream, a far larger indication than the approved 2L biliary label; (c) the balance of an anticipated ~$440M regulatory milestone slate across US/EU/Japan/China ($15M of it from BeOne on China approval). $27 is not a stretch mark - the stock traded $27-28 through late April and May 2026 on the priority-review news alone, and the 52-week high is $29.75.
- Lose leg $17 (board said $18). Arithmetic: $21.81 - $3.40 milestone = $18.41 before any value is taken off the deferred 1L royalty NPV; $17 leaves modest room for that. Not lower, because a CRL on a positive-OS Phase 3 with BTD is typically a manufacturing/label delay rather than a kill, and because the post-Theravance entity retains the YUPELRI annuity and the 2L Ziihera/BeOne royalties.
- EV: 0.85 x 27 + 0.15 x 17 = $25.50 vs $21.81 live = +16.9%. R:R = +$5.19 up / -$4.81 down = 1.08:1 on price, carried by probability rather than by payoff asymmetry.

The XBI-at-5-year-high caveat cuts the opposite way for this name: in a regime where market-implied win probabilities are generally rich, ZYME has faded 19% into its own dated binary, which is the anomaly worth explaining, not a discount to buy on faith.

LBTYK.thesis_summary: Liberty Global is a holding company trading at ~$10.64 (LBTYK, ~341m shares, ~$3.63bn market cap) whose resolving event is the spin-off of Ziggo Group — VodafoneZiggo (Netherlands) plus Telenet (Belgium), 13m customers, EUR6.6bn revenue — to be listed on Euronext Amsterdam in 2027, with Liberty Global distributing its 90% to shareholders tax-free for US holders. The structural precondition is now DONE: on 3 August 2026 the company completed the purchase of Vodafone's 50% of VodafoneZiggo for EUR1.0bn cash plus a 10% Ziggo Group stake, so there is no longer a JV partner, no approval contingency and no financing condition standing between here and the listing. The trade is the holdco discount closing: on management's own Q2 marks, guided year-end corporate cash of ~$2.0bn ($5.87/sh) plus the Liberty Growth portfolio at $2.9bn FMV ($8.50/sh) equals $14.37/sh with every telecom asset — 90% of Ziggo Group, 50% of Virgin Media O2, VM Ireland — carried at zero. The listing is the mechanism that forces the market to mark the telecom stub, exactly as the 2024 Sunrise spin did. It is genuinely idiosyncratic: nothing about the outcome depends on the tape, only on whether Liberty Global executes a distribution it has already restructured itself to make. What it is NOT is dated. There is no record date, no listing prospectus, no scheduled shareholder vote; guidance was tightened to "as early as mid-2027" in the 24 July Q2 release and then restated as plain "2027" in the 3 August completion release, and the board retains the right to abandon.
LBTYK.kill_risk: The most load-bearing claim in the thesis is that ~$2.0bn of holdco cash underwrites the downside. It is a forecast, not a balance, and I cannot bridge it from the live record. The Q2 10-Q reconciles exactly to the skeptic's read: consolidated cash $2,418.6m at 30 June 2026, of which only $1,610.1m "represented available liquidity at the corporate level" and $808.5m sits inside the Telenet and VM Ireland borrowing groups. The EUR1.0bn (~$1.15bn) Vodafone payment went out on 3 August, leaving roughly $0.46bn of corporate cash plus $76m of separately-managed-account investments. Getting to $2.0bn by 31 December therefore needs ~$1.5bn of further H2 inflows, and the disposals named to supply it — the 50% Wyre stake (guided only to year-end 2026 or Q1 2027), the VodafoneZiggo towers, Belgian and Dutch property, EUR1.2-1.4bn in total — are described in the company's own 3 August release as proceeds that "will be used to retire debt" at the subsidiaries, not upstreamed to the holding company. I could not determine from any primary source whether the Vodafone payment was funded from holdco cash or from the new Benelux debt (Wyre drew EUR2.71bn of a EUR4.35bn facility, upstreaming ~EUR2.38bn to Telenet, which then repaid EUR2.12bn of its own 2028 maturities); the two readings differ by more than a dollar a share on the floor. Compounding it: ~$340m of the $1.2bn of year-to-date "monetizations" is an asset-backed loan secured on the Wyre stake — borrowed money encumbering the very asset the next checkpoint depends on selling — and the 10-Q states no repurchase program is authorized for 2026, so there is no company bid to defend the discount before the spin. Second-order but real: the resolving event carries no binding date and the 3 August release dropped the "as early as mid-2027" qualifier the Q2 release had added, which is the shape a quiet slip takes before it is announced as one.

LBTYK.dossier_note:
CATALYST. Real, live, unfired, idiosyncratic, and materially de-risked since the board dossier was written. The 3 August 2026 completion of the VodafoneZiggo buyout (EUR1.0bn cash + 10% stake to Vodafone; Liberty Global at 90%) removes the last structural contingency: no JV partner, no pending approval, no financing condition. It is also not a slip - the dossier expected close "by 31 July", it landed 3 August. Not FIRED, because the buyout is preparatory; the resolving event is the distribution and Euronext Amsterdam listing of Ziggo Group, which has not happened. PENDING_SOFT rather than PENDING_HARD because nothing binds the date: the 24 July Q2 release said "the planned Ziggo Group spin-off as early as mid-2027", the 3 August release says only "list Ziggo Group in Amsterdam in 2027", and there is no record date, no prospectus and no scheduled vote. I set dated_milestone to null rather than carry the board's 2027-06-30, which was an invented mid-2027 proxy. The real dated waypoints, none of which resolve the trade: Stephen van Rooyen (CEO) and Jany Fruytier (CFO) take office 1 September 2026 with the rest of the leadership team named that month; the 50% Wyre stake sale guided to year-end 2026 or Q1 2027; EUR1.2-1.4bn of Belgian and Dutch disposals under way.

VALUATION - SoP, ~341m shares ($3.63bn market cap / $10.64). Three stacks, because the difference between them is the whole argument.

(1) Guided stack, which is where the board's $18 lives. Year-end-2026 corporate cash target ~$2.0bn = $5.87/sh, plus Liberty Growth at its Q2 FMV of $2.9bn = $8.50/sh, totals $14.37/sh with 90% of Ziggo Group, 50% of VMO2 and VM Ireland all carried at zero. This reconciles to management's own Q2 statement that cash plus growth marks exceed the share price by about 30% ($4.9bn vs $3.63bn = +35%). The board's $18 implies $6.14bn, i.e. $1.24bn or $3.64/sh for the entire telecom portfolio - roughly 0.2x revenue for the Ziggo equity alone against EUR6.6bn of revenue and ~EUR2.5bn of combined EBITDA. On that basis $18 is reproducible and, if anything, undemanding, so I keep it.

(2) Hard marks today, which the board number quietly assumes away. Corporate-level liquidity was $1,610.1m at 30 June (the 10-Q is explicit that only this slice is available at the corporate level; $808.5m of the $2,418.6m consolidated sits trapped in the Telenet and VM Ireland borrowing groups, and Liberty Global standalone held $0). Less the ~$1.15bn Vodafone payment made 3 August, plus $76m of separately-managed accounts, that is ~$0.54bn = $1.57/sh. Add Growth at full FMV and the stack is $3.44bn = $10.09/sh - approximately the share price. So the "HoldCo cash alone is 60% of market cap" framing circulating in sell-side and Seeking Alpha notes is a forward-dated claim, not a present balance. The bridge from $0.46bn to $2.0bn needs ~$1.5bn of H2 inflows from disposals the company's own 3 August release earmarks for retiring SUBSIDIARY debt.

(3) Floor. $0.46bn cash + $0.08bn SMA + Growth at a 25% haircut ($2.175bn) = $2.715bn = $7.96/sh, telecom at zero. At a 50% haircut it is $5.60/sh. The observed max-fear print is the 27 July close of $9.59 against a 52-week low of $9.30 - and note that low was set AFTER the spin was announced and after the cash target was raised, so it is not a stale pre-catalyst print. I set the floor at $7.50: below the 25%-haircut asset mark, above the punitive case, and materially below the board's $9.50, which was a chart level credited with guided cash. R:R at $10.64 falls from 6.45 to 2.34.

NOT APPLICABLE. Deck-mark gate: no commodity linkage, no feasibility study or price deck - the SoP rests on holdco cash, a venture portfolio marked to FMV, and levered European cable equity. Takeout lens: not a bio/pharma name; the 2026 biotech M&A regime is irrelevant here and I have not imported any takeout optionality into the target.

DRIVER. Spin_index_flow retained and confirmed - the mechanism is a distribution plus a new Euronext Amsterdam listing with the attendant index and holder-rotation flow, the same shape as the 2024 Sunrise spin the company explicitly cites as precedent. staging stays true: the event is real but undated, and roughly eleven-plus months distant at the earliest guided timing.

SKEPTIC PASS ON MYSELF. The claim I leaned hardest on is that cash and marks underwrite the downside. Attacked from the live record, it does not hold as stated - see kill_risk. Two further quality problems I could not clear: ~$340m of the $1.2bn of "monetizations" is an asset-backed loan against the Wyre stake, so leverage on the asset the next checkpoint depends on selling is being counted as cash raised; and the 10-Q states no share repurchase program is authorized for 2026, so no company bid exists to close the discount before the listing. Unresolved fact I flag rather than guess: I could not establish from any primary source whether the EUR1.0bn Vodafone payment was funded from holdco cash or from the new Benelux debt (Wyre drew EUR2.71bn of a EUR4.35bn facility, upstreaming ~EUR2.38bn to Telenet, which repaid EUR2.12bn of 2028 maturities). If it came from the Benelux structure, the floor is roughly a dollar-plus per share higher than I have marked it and the $2.0bn bridge is far less strained. SEC full-text retrieval returned 403 in this environment, so the 10-Q line items above are reconciled arithmetically ($1,610.1m + $808.5m = $2,418.6m) rather than re-read directly - worth one primary-source confirmation before sizing.

VIR.thesis_summary: Vir is a binary on ECLIPSE 1, the fully-enrolled registrational Phase 3 of tobevibart + elebsiran in chronic hepatitis delta, with topline guided by the company to Q4 2026 - an idiosyncratic, un-fired, dated readout backed by Phase 2 SOLSTICE data showing 77% HDV RNA target-not-detected at week 72 rising to 88% at week 96. The company is funded past the event (cash, equivalents and investments $809.3M at 31 Mar 2026, plus $315M of Astellas closing proceeds in April, runway guided into H2 2028), so the loss leg is a cash-box mark rather than a financing accident; the fragile axis is not the trial's odds but what a win is commercially worth in a small, diagnosis-bottlenecked indication.
VIR.dated_milestone: ECLIPSE 1 Phase 3 chronic hepatitis delta topline expected Q4 2026 (company guidance restated in the Q1 2026 corporate update, 6 May 2026: "Topline data from the Phase 3 ECLIPSE 1 trial are expected in the fourth quarter of 2026"); ECLIPSE 2 and ECLIPSE 3 topline Q1 2027. ECLIPSE 1 enrollment completed 3 Nov 2025. Nearer checkpoints: Q2 2026 results call 5 Aug 2026 (next chance to re-guide) and VIR-5818 HER2 response data in H2 2026.
VIR.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim is the $19 win leg, not the trial odds - and the tape argues against it. At $8.90 with a $3.5 floor, the market implies only ~35% for a fully-enrolled Phase 3 whose Phase 2 printed 88% HDV RNA TND at week 96; if the win leg were really $19 at a 60-70% probability of success the stock would not sit here. The honest residual is commercial, not clinical: chronic hepatitis delta is diagnosis-bottlenecked, and Gilead's bulevirtide - the only approved HDV agent anywhere - has been a modest commercial performer, so a clean ECLIPSE 1 win may re-rate toward $13-15 rather than $19. Compounding it, the Q4 2026 event is ONE of three registrational trials; a filing package needs ECLIPSE 2/3 in Q1 2027, so the dated catalyst only partially de-risks and a positive-but-noisy print can be sold. Two live timing risks: guidance was Q1 2027 topline as recently as the 3 Nov 2025 enrollment release before being pulled into Q4 2026, and the 5 Aug 2026 Q2 call is an unhedged opportunity to push it back - with an interim principal financial officer in the seat since 23 July 2026.

VIR.dossier_note:
CATALYST REALITY. Real, forward-dated, unfired, idiosyncratic. ECLIPSE 1 (tobevibart + elebsiran, chronic hepatitis delta) completed enrollment 3 Nov 2025; the company's 6 May 2026 corporate update states topline is expected in Q4 2026, with ECLIPSE 2/3 topline in Q1 2027. No press release, filing or news item between 6 May and 3 Aug 2026 alters that - the only company news since is the 22 July Q2 call notice, the 24 July CFO transition (Jason O'Byrne out 3 Aug; Brent Sabatini interim principal financial officer from 23 July), and a 10 June board appointment. PENDING_HARD, staging=false, driver unchanged (FDA_clinical_readout).

DIRECTION OF TRAVEL - not a slip. The 3 Nov 2025 release read: "The last patient in ECLIPSE 1 is expected to reach the trial's primary endpoint (primary completion date) in the fourth quarter of 2026, with topline data expected in the first quarter of 2027." The 6 May 2026 release reads: "Topline data from the Phase 3 ECLIPSE 1 trial are expected in the fourth quarter of 2026." That is a pull-forward, and the more recent company statement governs. Flagging it so the CRO does not read a stale Q1-2027 citation as a slip.

WIN LEG ARITHMETIC ($19, held). Success-case sum-of-parts on ~168.7M shares: de-risked-but-pre-approval HDV franchise ~$2.0B (street peak-sales work clusters near $1-1.5B WW for a finite-duration functional-cure regimen launching 2028) + ~$0.76B cash at readout + ~$0.45B for retained oncology (VIR-5500 partnered with Astellas: $1.37B of remaining development/regulatory/sales milestones plus tiered double-digit ex-US royalties, Astellas funding development; plus wholly-owned VIR-5818 HER2 and VIR-5525 EGFR TCEs) = ~$3.2B, or $19.0/sh. Independent corroboration, not substitution: sell-side consensus target $21.71, median $20.00, range $18-30.

LOSS LEG ARITHMETIC ($3.5, corrected from board $4.8). Full derivation in discrepancies[]. Short form: ~$1,144M funded at 31 Mar 2026 including Astellas, less ~$390M of burn to a Q4 2026 readout = ~$755M gross = $4.48/sh; less ~$148M of lease, contingent-consideration and other claims = ~$3.60/sh net; the tape's own precedent multiple is 0.75x GROSS cash (the $4.155 low against $777.4M of cash on 139.5M shares at 31 Dec 2025), which maps to $3.36. Floor $3.5.

R:R AT SPOT $8.90. Upside $10.10, downside $5.40 = 1.87:1 (board's implied 4.8 floor would have shown 2.6:1). Breakeven probability 34.8%. At win_prob 0.55, EV = 0.55*19 + 0.45*3.5 = $12.03, or +35% vs spot.

TAKEOUT LENS - optionality only, NO lift applied. If ECLIPSE 1 reads out clean, Vir holds the only functional-cure combination in an indication where the sole approved agent anywhere is Gilead's bulevirtide (EU only; the US filing drew a CRL), which makes Gilead the obvious strategic and GSK - Vir's former sotrovimab partner with standing hepatitis-B ambitions - the second. I could NOT verify a named, dated, valued 2026 comparable takeout in hepatology within this pass, so per the deck rule the win-leg target is NOT lifted for M&A; treat takeout as undated optionality stacked on the dated readout, never as the event. Cutting the other way: with XBI at multi-year highs, the $4.155 max-fear print used to anchor the floor multiple is a late-2025/early-2026 tape artifact and may be stale-low - which makes $3.5 the conservative end rather than the central case. A failure, however, would manufacture its own fresh max-fear tape, which is why the conservative end is the one published.

OUT OF SCOPE, FLAGGED: Q2 2026 results land 5 Aug 2026 after the close (consensus revenue ~$135.9M, EPS +$0.33, both reflecting Astellas recognition) - the CRO owns whether to underwrite through that print.

OLMA.thesis_summary: Olema is a single-asset binary on OPERA-01, the pivotal Phase 3 of palazestrant (oral CERAN/SERD) as monotherapy versus standard-of-care endocrine therapy in ER+/HER2- metastatic breast cancer after endocrine therapy plus a CDK4/6 inhibitor (NCT06015738/NCT06016738, 510 patients, dual PFS primary endpoint read in the ESR1-mutant and the all-comers intent-to-treat populations by blinded central review). The event is real, forward-dated, unfired and idiosyncratic: no company press release since routine inducement grants on 2 July 2026, no 8-K since the 23 June 2026 annual-meeting filing, no topline, no offering, no slippage notice. The only written timing statement retrievable is the 12 May 2026 Q1 release, "top-line data anticipated this fall" - a season, guided by event accrual, with no regulator or counterparty clock, so this is PENDING_SOFT, not PENDING_HARD. The next hard date is the Q2 report on 10 August 2026, which will either restate or soften the fall window. The board's two-point payoff ($24 up, $6.50 down) is not reproducible from the live record; on the correct economic share base and burn-adjusted cash the honest structure is three legs, and the blended expected value sits on top of the current price.
OLMA.dated_milestone: OPERA-01 pivotal Phase 3 topline, guided to "fall 2026" (company Q1 release 12 May 2026; reaffirmed at the Goldman Sachs 47th Annual Global Healthcare Conference fireside chat 9 June 2026, occurrence confirmed but content not retrievable from a primary record). Window, not a date. Nearest hard date is the Q2 2026 report on 10 August 2026 (FMP earnings calendar, EPS est -0.53), the restate-or-soften checkpoint.
OLMA.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim is that a positive OPERA-01 is worth roughly $24-25. It is only worth that if the all-comers ITT arm wins, and every oral SERD to date has won in ESR1-mutant patients and struggled or failed in ESR1-wildtype: Roche's giredestrant flopped in first line, vepdegestrant hit ESR1m but missed ITT, EMERALD's ITT effect was thin. Meanwhile the ESR1m niche palazestrant would win into is already commercially occupied - imlunestrant FDA-approved September 2025 (EMBER-3), elacestrant approved 2023, camizestrant approved in the EU in 2026 with a CDK4/6 inhibitor. So the most likely "success" headline (ESR1m PFS hit, ITT miss or borderline) lands into a crowded second-line market and is worth roughly $9-10, i.e. flat to down from $11.28. Second, the spread is already gone: my own three-leg lattice prices the stock at $11.28-11.30 against a $11.28 close, i.e. zero expectation edge, nowhere near the 25-30% margin this book requires. Third, the fall window is self-guided on PFS-event accrual with registry NCT06016738 last showing RECRUITING with 510 ESTIMATED (not actual) enrollment, so a slip into 1H 2027 costs another ~$110m of burn against the floor with no counterparty obliged to act.

DBVT.dossier_note: This is a real event on a genuinely improved asset, and it is still not the trade this funnel exists to fund. Take the good news at full weight first. The December 2025 pivotal trial cleared its bar at the lower edge of its confidence interval, not its midpoint -- 46.6% of treated children responding against 14.8% on placebo, with the conservative edge of the effect at 24.5 points against a 15-point requirement. Compliance was 96.2%, which speaks directly to the adhesion failure that ended the 2020 cycle. The FDA has asked for no additional data. The only approved competitor is being withdrawn from the market on 31 July 2026. None of that is spin, and a director should not dismiss it. But the discipline this lane applies is about the shape of the bet, not the merit of the science, and on that test three things fail. CELC.dossier_note: This seat existed for one reason: a dated regulatory decision with a spread between the live price and the value the decision would unlock. That decision fired on 14 July 2026, three days early, and it went our way. The position is nonetheless down about 46% from the high. That single fact settles the question this funnel is meant to answer. The discipline here is not to be clever about it. A catalyst that has already resolved is spent, whichever way it resolved. The asymmetry we were paid to underwrite - a hard date, a binding decision, a bounded loss - no longer exists in this name. What remains is a commercial-launch story: whether a first-time commercial company can ship on time, whether oncologists will accept a regimen that produced mouth sores in 58 to 72% of trial patients, and whether a second label arrives before the competition does. Those are perfectly respectable questions. They are not event-driven questions, and they cannot be answered before the first revenue line arrives in early November 2026. The second finding is the one that decides the sizing. The downside floor of $60 carried on the board is not a floor. It is a bear valuation that already assumes the launch broadly works - at $60 the enterprise is worth about $2.79B, which needs peak annual sales above $1.2B. The only hard number underneath is net cash of roughly $140M, about $3 a share. There is no acquirer under contract, no contingent payment right, no recovery value. A defensible adverse case is $5

AQST.kill_risk: The HF validation study must prove error-free self-administration of exactly the behavior FDA flagged (administration sequence/mouth-drying); a redesign-recycle there kills the Q3 timeline and possibly the label. Nearer-term: no resubmission announced with ~8 weeks left in the guided quarter - a slip past 9/30 flips this to SLIPPED and the new S-3 shelf (effective 7/8/2026) gives management dilution capacity into any weakness. A securities class action (class period 6/16/2025-1/8/2026) alleging misleading FDA-communication disclosure adds credibility tax to management's own timeline guidance.

WVE.thesis_summary: Wave Life Sciences holds an FDA-GRANTED, not-yet-held meeting to discuss a potential accelerated-approval pathway for WVE-006 (GalNAc RNA editing) in alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency. Verified verbatim in the 30 July 2026 Q2 release: the meeting request "was granted by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA)" and "is scheduled for the end of summer 2026." The event is real, idiosyncratic (resolves on Wave's own AAT biomarker package and FDA judgement, not the tape), and UNFIRED as of 4 August 2026 - but it has slipped a full quarter (Wave's 18 May 2026 release guided "regulatory feedback ... mid-2026"), it is season-dated rather than calendar-dated, it is non-binding (minutes and guidance, no decision, no payout), and minutes customarily arrive ~30 days post-meeting, pointing disclosure into the company's own "investor day in the fall of 2026." The load-bearing asymmetry is not probability but PAYOFF: Beam Therapeutics already secured FDA alignment on a biomarker-based accelerated pathway for BEAM-302 in the same indication on 25 March 2026 (12-month AAT biomarker endpoint, 60 mg dose), so a favourable Wave answer is confirmation of an established agency precedent, not a revelation. Re-derived on live numbers the name prices roughly at fair value: 0.45 x $7.75 + 0.55 x $4.10 = $5.74 versus a $5.74 last, i.e. essentially zero expected edge, against the board's +20.6%.
WVE.kill_risk: The most load-bearing claim in the thesis is that a favourable FDA answer pays. It may not. Three live facts push against it. (1) PRECEDENT ALREADY SET: Beam obtained FDA alignment on an AAT-biomarker accelerated pathway for BEAM-302 on 25 March 2026, so "FDA open to biomarker AA in AATD" is priced knowledge; Wave winning re-rates the company only to the extent its own levels look competitive. (2) THEY DO NOT: on Wave's own 18 May 2026 numbers, functional wild-type M-AAT is 11.9 uM x 64.4% = 7.7 uM (200 mg biweekly) and 13.6 uM x 58.7% = 8.0 uM (400 mg monthly) - both BELOW the ~11 uM augmentation-therapy protective threshold, versus Beam's 16.1 uM total at 94% M-AAT = ~15.1 uM functional. The agency can grant the endpoint class and still require a dose/level Wave has not yet shown, which converts a "win" into a reset timeline pending the 600 mg monthly cohort. (3) NO CLEAN DISCLOSURE EVENT: minutes are private, ~30 days post-meeting, and the company's stated venue is a fall investor day - Wave controls both the timing and the framing, so the "resolution" can arrive as a bundled narrative slide rather than a printable answer. Residual: the position can be right on the science and still collect no repricing.

AMLX.thesis_summary: Amylyx Pharmaceuticals is a single-asset binary into the Phase 3 LUCIDITY topline for avexitide (first-in-class GLP-1 receptor antagonist, FDA Breakthrough Therapy) in post-bariatric hypoglycemia, company-guided to Q3 2026 and reaffirmed in the 7 May 2026 Q1 release. Enrollment closed March 2026 at 78 participants against a 16-week FDA-agreed primary endpoint (composite rate of Level 2 and Level 3 hypoglycemic events), so the last Week-16 visit fell ~mid-July and the print is mechanically due. Verified unfired as of 2026-08-04: latest 8-K is 4 June 2026, latest substantive press release 23 June 2026 (Phase 1 LUMINA ALS at ENCALS), and the only newer item is an 3 Aug 2026 notice that Q2 results come 6 August 2026. The event is fully idiosyncratic - it resolves on trial data, not on the tape. The correction versus the board is on the axes, not the catalyst: the stock has re-rated to $20.17 (52-week range $7.48-$20.94, 200-day $14.83), the downside leg is net cash of roughly $2.13/share at 30 June, not $4, and on a defensible $30 win leg the market-implied win probability is already ~64% - at or above my own ~62% estimate. The asymmetry this funnel hunts existed near $8; what remains is a fairly-priced coin flip with an 88% loss leg.
AMLX.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim is "an unfired, mechanically-due pivotal binary with defined downside". Both halves are attackable from the live record. (1) The price has already discounted the win: on my legs the breakeven probability is (20.17-2.50)/(30-2.50) = 64.3%, above my 62% fundamental estimate, so the expected value is roughly flat-to-slightly-negative rather than the +45% the board carries - the edge was in the $8-14 tape, not at a 52-week high. (2) The evidentiary prior is thinner than "pivotal-ready" implies: the supporting work is a Phase 2 PREVENT crossover of N=18 (40-55% event reduction) and an N=16 open-label investigator-initiated Phase 2b; a 78-patient parallel-group read on a variable, event-count endpoint with real placebo response is not the same experiment, and Breakthrough designation is not evidence of effect size. (3) The downside is not defined in any protective sense: the same management team's prior binary (AMX0035 PHOENIX) closed $18.97 on 7 Mar 2024 and $3.36 on 8 Mar 2024, -82% in one session, resting at $1.62 by June 2024 - and that shell held more cash per share than AMLX will hold at the LUCIDITY print, so $2.50 is a mark, not a floor; $1.60-2.00 is inside precedent. (4) Timing residual: "Q3 2026" is a company-guided quarter window, not a PDUFA-style binding date, and slip into Q4 is possible - the 6 August 2026 Q2 call is the next checkpoint that would confirm or break the September end-stop.

AGIO.kill_risk: Voxelotor precedent: Pfizer withdrew Oxbryta worldwide on 2024-09-25 after an accelerated approval built on the SAME hemoglobin-response surrogate showed higher VOC rates and deaths in post-marketing data. In RISE UP, annualized sickle-cell pain crises were only numerically lower and did NOT reach statistical significance - the exact pattern that discredited the surrogate. FDA can therefore demand clinical-benefit (VOC/transfusion) evidence rather than Hb response, issue a CRL, or convene a late advisory committee (none announced as of 2026-08-04, ~90 days out - an AdCom notice would itself be a de-rating event). Agios' own 2026 record cuts against the class story: tebapivat failed in LR-MDS (2026-05-29) and was dropped in SCD (2026-07-21) for want of a differentiated profile, and a Pomerantz securities investigation opened 2026-07-28/30 on that disclosure. Secondary risk: an approval print may land nearer $36-40 with the balance of the $45 earned only on launch execution, so a "win" may not pay the full win leg by the event date.

SVRA.thesis_summary: Savara is a single-asset binary on the FDA approval of MOLBREEVI (molgramostim inhalation solution, inhaled recombinant GM-CSF delivered via PARI's eFlow nebulizer) for autoimmune pulmonary alveolar proteinosis - which would be the first and only approved therapy in the indication. Efficacy is settled: IMPALA-2 hit its primary endpoint (change in hemoglobin-adjusted %-predicted DLCO at Wk24) and multiple secondaries, with LS-mean DLCO +11.6pp vs +4.7pp placebo at Wk48 (p<0.001) and SGRQ-T -11.5 vs -4.9 at Wk24 (p=0.007), published and presented through ATS 2026. BLA is under Priority Review with Fast Track, Breakthrough and Orphan designations and NO advisory committee. The resolving event is the PDUFA action date, which is idiosyncratic and forward-dated - but it is 2026-11-22, not the board's 2026-08-22: the FDA deemed Savara's responses to information requests a major amendment and extended the review three months (announced 2026-04-15). The residual question is not whether the drug works; it is whether the manufacturing/device dossier clears, in a program that has already been refused-to-file once on exactly that.
SVRA.kill_risk: CMC/drug-device manufacturing, not efficacy, is the live failure mode - and it has already bitten this program once. Refuting my own load-bearing claim ("efficacy is settled so approval is near-certain"): the FDA issued a Refusal to File on 2025-05-27 because the March-2025 BLA was not complete enough for substantive review, specifically requesting additional Chemistry, Manufacturing and Controls data (stock -32% that day, 25M shares, $2.93 to $1.94). The file was only resubmitted in Dec-2025 and filed in Feb-2026. Now, mid-review, FDA information requests have again triggered a major amendment and a three-month clock reset. For an inhaled biologic dependent on a third-party device partner (PARI eFlow), the approvable gate is CMC/device/facility inspection, and that gate has a demonstrated history of catching this sponsor. Note also that "the FDA did not cite any safety, efficacy, or manufacturing concerns" is the company's characterisation of correspondence, not an FDA statement of approvability - and management's regulatory-readiness disclosures are themselves the subject of a securities class action filed Sept-2025 (Rosen, E.D. Pa.) over the prior BLA. A CMC CRL is resolvable in 6-12 months but destroys the dated event and, from a $1.09B market cap now substantially priced for approval, costs far more than the RTF did off a ~$490M base.

RARE.thesis_summary: Ultragenyx carries two dated, statutory FDA action dates 27 days apart on the same AAV manufacturing platform: DTX401 (pariglasgene brecaparvovec, AAV8 for Glycogen Storage Disease Ia) has a Priority Review PDUFA of 2026-08-23 with NO advisory committee anticipated, and UX111 (rebisufligene etisparvovec, AAV9 for Sanfilippo A/MPS IIIA) has a PDUFA of 2026-09-19 following a July-2025 CMC/facility-inspection CRL and an accepted resubmission. Both would be first-ever therapies in their indications. The event is idiosyncratic (a CBER approval decision on company-specific CMC and clinical files) and unfired. The setrusumab risk that dominated this name is already SPENT, not pending: Orbit and Cosmic both missed the annualized-fracture primary endpoint on 2025-12-29, which is what reset the stock from ~$40 and spawned the pending securities suits — it is not a forward risk to this catalyst. Structure is a levered binary: ~98.5M shares against ~$666M net debt and negative book equity, so equity moves ~1.2x any enterprise-value move in either direction.
RARE.kill_risk: The win leg can be approved-but-not-paid. DTX401's Phase 3 primary endpoint was reduction in daily cornstarch intake — a management-burden endpoint, not hard morbidity — in a disease already controlled with cheap cornstarch, and GSDIa is ultra-rare (~1:100,000). A ~$3M one-time gene therapy on that evidence invites narrow labeling and slow payer uptake, so FDA approval on 2026-08-23 can land without the ~$531M of EV the $30 target requires. That matters more than usual here because the balance sheet is not forgiving: ~$540M of cash and investments against ~$136M/quarter operating burn (Q4-25 $752M to Q1-26 $540M, adjusted for $76M of debt paydown) puts runway into roughly mid-2027 with $1.2B of debt and negative stockholders' equity, so a slow-monetizing approval still leaves a dilutive raise in front of the stock. Second-order and correlated: a repeat CMC CRL would hit both PDUFAs, since UX111's July-2025 CRL cited facility inspection observations at the same manufacturing organization that supplies DTX401 — the two dates are not independent draws.

CMCSA.thesis_summary: Comcast announced 2026-06-29 (8-K Ex-99.1) its intention to separate into two public companies via a tax-free spin-off of NBCUniversal + Sky, "expected to be completed in approximately one year" (i.e. ~mid-2027). RemainCo = domestic broadband/wireless/business services on the 65m-home converged network (Michael Angelakis CEO); SpinCo = Universal parks/studios, NBC/Telemundo, Peacock, Bravo and Sky (Mike Cavanagh CEO). The trade is a sum-of-the-parts re-rate: the consolidated entity trades at ~4.85x EV/EBITDA (EV $169.9B on $87.2B cap + $82.7B Q2-2026 net debt, over ~$35B FY26E adjusted EBITDA), while the live comps are CHTR at 5.70x and DIS at 10.81x EV/EBITDA TTM. Marking the parts at 5.5x / 7.5x on 2027E gets ~$34/sh vs $24.56 spot. Carry is paid by the $0.33/qtr dividend declared 2026-07-23 (5.4% yield, covered ~3.5x by H1-26 FCF of $8.5B).
CMCSA.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim is "the parts re-rate." Three live facts cut against it. (1) Comcast just ran this experiment: the Versant spin closed 2026-01-02 and the stub went from a $32.86 52-wk high to a $21.28 low - a spin at this issuer has already failed once in seven months to re-rate the remainder. (2) The EBITDA base is eroding faster than the multiple is likely to expand: Q2-26 residential C&P adjusted EBITDA fell 8.0% y/y, domestic broadband revenue -5.5%, 167k broadband subs lost in the quarter, and total adjusted EBITDA fell 5.3% y/y even pro forma for Versant/Sky-Germany. A 23-month hold against a -5%/yr base eats most of a one-turn re-rate. (3) The Disney-multiple analogue is structurally blocked: the 8-K states NBCUniversal will carry "the same dual-class share structure as Comcast" (Roberts control retained) and Comcast keeps up to 19.9% of SpinCo to monetize over time - a governance discount plus a stated overhang, against a single-class DIS comp. Deal risk is also non-trivial and self-declared: final board approval, tax opinions, regulatory approvals and financing are all still outstanding, with "no assurance that the proposed transaction will be completed." Finally, the driver is only semi-idiosyncratic - completion resolves on company facts, but the realized value depends on where the tape chooses to multiple cable and legacy media in mid-2027.

GLUE.thesis_summary: Monte Rosa (GLUE, $15.38, $1.30B cap) is a clinical-stage molecular-glue-degrader company whose resolving event is the readout of the EXPANDED GFORCE-1 Phase 1 cohort of MRT-8102 (NEK7-directed MGD, NLRP3/IL-1b/IL-18 axis) in elevated-CVD-risk subjects, company-guided to H2 2026 and still unfired. The January 2026 interim already showed an 85% median hsCRP reduction with 94% of subjects driven below 2 mg/L and no infection signal, so the expansion is largely CONFIRMATORY on the biomarker rather than discovery. The event is idiosyncratic (resolves on GLUE's own trial data), the balance sheet is not a variable ($666M cash+ST investments at 3/31/26, guided runway into 2029), and the option value sits in three additional shots: MRT-6160 (VAV1) partnered to Novartis with multiple Phase 2 starts pending, MRT-2359 (GSPT1) entering Phase 2 in mCRPC in Q3 2026, and a CCNE1 IND in H2 2026. What the board did not know: on 2026-07-31 Novo Nordisk's Phase 3 ZEUS trial of ziltivekimab MISSED, with complete IL-6/hsCRP target engagement delivering MACE HR 0.99 (95% CI 0.88-1.11) in ASCVD+CKD+inflammation. GLUE fell ~28-30% on that read-across (roughly $24 on 1 July to $15.38 today, versus a $20.78 50-day average). ZEUS does not invalidate GLUE's own readout, but it devalues its payoff: the surrogate GLUE is about to report on is the same surrogate ZEUS just dissociated from clinical outcome. The catalyst survives; the prize behind it does not survive intact.
GLUE.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim in the thesis is that a positive expanded GFORCE-1 hsCRP readout is a value-creating de-risking event. The live record refutes it directly: ZEUS (2026-07-31) showed that TOTAL suppression of the IL-6/hsCRP axis produced MACE HR 0.99 in exactly the elevated-CVD-risk population GLUE is enrolling. GLUE's readout measures the same surrogate, so the event can resolve maximally positive and still produce no re-rate, or a "so what" fade. Two further live risks: (1) IL-1-pathway blockade carries a class serious-infection signal, seen on active drug in ZEUS, and a larger/longer expansion cohort is materially more likely to surface it than the small interim was; (2) the H2 2026 window is soft and the 2026-08-06 Q2 call could re-scope or defer the elevated-atherosclerotic-risk Phase 2, which would convert this to SLIPPED. The partial defense (CANTOS with canakinumab, an IL-1b agent upstream of IL-6, DID hit MACE at HR 0.85, so the ZEUS read-across is mechanistically arguable) is real but weak collateral: CANTOS never won FDA approval, its effect size was small, and no small-cap will fund a CV outcomes trial to prove the distinction.

GLUE.dossier_note:
WHAT CHANGED SINCE THE BOARD SCAN (2026-06-08). On 2026-07-31 Novo Nordisk disclosed that Phase 3 ZEUS (ziltivekimab, anti-IL-6, >6,300 patients with ASCVD + CKD + elevated hsCRP) missed its primary MACE endpoint: HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.88-1.11, DESPITE confirmed target engagement and the expected falls in free IL-6 and hsCRP, with more frequent serious infections on active. GLUE fell ~28-30% on the read-across (~$24.02 close 2026-07-01 -> $15.38 on 2026-08-04, -6.9% today alone; 50d avg $20.78, 200d avg $18.16, 52w range $4.12-$25.77). This is a biomarker-outcome dissociation event, and it lands on the exact surrogate GLUE is about to report.

CATALYST REALITY. The resolving event is REAL, FORWARD, UNFIRED and IDIOSYNCRATIC: the expanded GFORCE-1 Phase 1 cohort of MRT-8102 in elevated-CVD-risk subjects, guided in the Q1 2026 release (2026-05-07) to H2 2026. No SEC filing since a Form 4 on 2026-07-17 and no press release since 2026-07-02 (inducement grants) - the company has NOT publicly responded to ZEUS. Status is PENDING_SOFT, not PENDING_HARD: "H2 2026" is a window, not a binding date. Not FIRED (expansion has not read out); not BROKEN (ZEUS was a different company, a different molecule and a downstream node - it damaged the payoff, not the trial). Caveat on idiosyncrasy: the 07-31 move demonstrates this name carries large mechanism-class beta that the "resolves on its own facts" test does not capture.

TAKEOUT LENS - NOT APPLIED, deliberately. The 2026 M&A regime (37 biotechs >=$1B YTD, ~$216B) rewards LATE-STAGE, commercially-ready assets. GLUE has no pivotal data in hand and nothing near approval: MRT-8102 is Phase 1 with Phase 2 starts still ahead, MRT-2359 enters Phase 2 in Q3'26, and its most partnerable asset (MRT-6160) is already licensed to Novartis - which removes it from the auction rather than advertising it. ZEUS also just cooled strategic appetite for CV-inflammation specifically. No comp supports a takeout premium here, so I have not lifted the win leg by a dollar on it. The regime's other edge applies too: with XBI near five-year highs, market-implied win probabilities in biotech are RICHER than historical, which argues against, not for, paying up for a soft-dated surrogate readout.

FOR THE CRO: this is no longer an asymmetric bet, it is roughly a coin flip with slightly worse-than-even payoff. Watch 2026-08-06 - if management firms the H2 2026 readout AND holds the elevated-atherosclerotic-risk Phase 2 start, status can move toward PENDING_HARD; if either is deferred or re-scoped, this becomes SLIPPED and the edge_grade H the board assigned (built on a pre-ZEUS 3.79 payoff) is no longer supportable.

IMTX.thesis_summary: Immatics is a binary on the SUPRAME Phase 3 of anzu-cel (anzutresgene autoleucel, IMA203), a PRAME TCR-T cell therapy randomized against investigator's choice in previously-treated (post-PD-1) advanced cutaneous melanoma, primary endpoint BICR-assessed PFS. The company guides that the pre-specified interim AND final analyses are "expected to be triggered in 2026" on accrual of a defined number of PFS events, feeding a BLA in 1H 2027 and first commercial launch in 2027 (Q1-2026 update, 12 May 2026; repeated in the 1 June 2026 ASCO release: "Phase 3 SUPRAME trial remains on track"). The event is unfired as of 04 Aug 2026 - no 6-K or press release since the 17 Jul 2026 ESMO notice, and none of the three ESMO (23-27 Oct, Madrid) presentations contains SUPRAME data (they are Ph1b anzu-cel durability, Ph1 IMA203CD8, Ph1b IMA402). It is idiosyncratic: the trigger is the trial's own event count, not the tape. Supporting evidence for the win leg is mature Ph1b RP2D data - 56% cORR, 14.6mo mDOR, 6.1mo mPFS, 16.2mo mOS in heavily pretreated metastatic melanoma - against an investigator's-choice control arm that historically runs ~2-3mo PFS in this setting. Balance sheet is not a constraint into the readout: EUR454.0M cash + short-term investments at 31 Mar 2026 ($521.5M at the company's own FX), no funded debt, runway guided into 2028.
IMTX.kill_risk: Load-bearing claim under test: that the Ph1b RP2D efficacy (56% cORR / 6.1mo mPFS) carries into a randomized ITT comparison. It may not. The Ph1b cohort is doubly selected - HLA-A*02:01-positive AND PRAME-positive AND fit enough to survive apheresis, ~4-6 weeks of manufacturing and lymphodepletion before infusion - which imports an immortal-time/fitness bias that a randomized ITT Phase 3 strips out; the closest commercial analog, Iovance's lifileucel, converted strong single-arm melanoma data into a far weaker commercial reality. Second, timing: the trigger is event-driven, and the "2026" guidance has been carried forward verbatim from the FY-2025 update through Q1-2026 without ever being narrowed - so a slip into 2027 (which would spend time-value without resolving anything) is a live path, not a tail. Third, structural: the near-term interim does NOT resolve the binary in the downside direction - an interim that misses efficacy does not stop the trial, it defers to the final analysis, so a "no" print likely lands the stock in the $6-7 zone rather than at the $4 terminal floor. Only a final-analysis miss produces the modeled $4.

The board tagged the wrong node of the chain.

IMTX.dossier_note:
CATALYST. Confirmed real, forward-dated, unfired, idiosyncratic. SUPRAME (NCT06743126) randomizes post-PD-1 advanced cutaneous melanoma to anzu-cel vs investigator's choice, primary endpoint BICR-assessed PFS; company guides interim AND final analyses "expected to be triggered in 2026" on a defined PFS event count, BLA 1H 2027, launch 2027. No SUPRAME news since; the 17 Jul 2026 ESMO notice covers only Ph1/Ph1b assets (anzu-cel durability poster 24 Oct, IMA203CD8 oral 23 Oct, IMA402 rapid oral 24 Oct) - so ESMO is NOT the resolving venue and must not be mistaken for one. SEC record 01 May - 04 Aug 2026 shows only routine 6-K/S-8/Form 3-4 traffic, no material disclosure. Next scheduled company communication: Q2 print 12 Aug 2026 (consensus -$0.484 EPS) - a guidance-refresh, not the event.

DRIVER CORRECTION (the material one). Board had FDA_approval_decision. That is wrong by roughly two years: the approval decision follows a BLA guided for 1H 2027. The thing that resolves this position in the next few quarters is a clinical readout. Retag FDA_clinical_readout. This matters for the <=2-per-driver cap - IMTX should compete against other readouts, not against PDUFA names.

SHARE COUNT / CASH (basis for both axes). Common stock EUR1,368,425 at EUR0.01 par at 31 Mar 2026 = ~136.8M shares; FMP market cap $1,209.6M / $9.02 implies 134.1M (stale count). Use ~135-137M. Cash + short-term investments EUR454.0M at 31 Mar 2026 = $521.5M at the company's own translation = ~$3.81/sh; total debt is EUR15.1M of leases only, so net cash ~$504M = ~$3.70/sh. Burn: Q3->Q4 2025 was EUR37M/qtr, Q1 2026 only EUR15M (flattered by collaboration receipts incl. a $5M Moderna milestone in Jan 2026); model ~EUR30M/qtr. Carried to 31 Dec 2026: ~EUR395M ~ $455M ~ $3.33/sh.

DOWNSIDE FLOOR = 4. Arithmetic: $3.33/sh year-end net cash + ~$0.65/sh residual for the non-anzu-cel estate (IMA402 PRAME TCER with Ph1b RP2D data due 2H 2026, IMA401 MAGEA4/8 with Ph1 published in Nature Medicine 31 May 2026, plus the BMS and Moderna collaborations) = ~$4.00. Honest caveat: that is ~1.2x net cash, the generous end. Busted-lead biotechs routinely clear at 0.7-1.0x cash, which would be $2.70-3.40. I keep 4 because the residual here is genuinely partnered and clinically live, but the CRO should treat 4 as the optimistic edge of a $3.00-4.00 terminal-failure band. Separately - and this is a real structural correction to the binary framing - the near-term interim cannot deliver the $4 case. An interim that fails to cross the efficacy boundary does not stop the trial, it defers to the final analysis; the realistic mark on that print is ~$6-7, not $4. The $4 requires a final-analysis miss. The 52-week low of $5.05 is consistent with this: the tape has never actually priced terminal failure.

FAIR VALUE TARGET = 20. At $20 x ~136M shares = $2.72B market cap, less ~$0.46B year-end cash = ~$2.26B EV for an approved-path first-in-class PRAME TCR-T in 2L+ melanoma plus the bispecific franchise. Corroborated by live consensus: analyst target $20.80 across 8 firms (30 Jul 2026, 6 buy / 1 hold / 1 sell). Kept at the round 20 rather than 20.80 to avoid importing sell-side precision the trial cannot support.

IMPLIED PROBABILITY CHECK. On axes 4 / 20 at the live $9.02, the market implies (9.02-4)/(20-4) = 31.4%. Board's 45% is the entire edge. EV = 0.45(20) + 0.55(4) = $11.20, i.e. +24.2% vs spot - reproduces the board's ev_pct 0.2417 exactly, and payoff 20/9.02 = 2.19 reproduces the board's payoff. Note the XBI-at-five-year-high caveat cuts against us here: in a hot tape, market-implied win probabilities are richer, so a 31.4% implied is if anything a *generous* read of how cheap the option is.

TAKEOUT LENS (undated optionality only - NOT a milestone, and it does not extend or substitute for the readout). Anzu-cel does not yet have pivotal data in hand, so IMTX is not today a "commercially-ready" takeout asset; it becomes one the day SUPRAME reads out positive. Strategic scarcity is genuine - it is the only randomized Phase 3 PRAME-directed cell therapy, in an HLA-restricted modality few can replicate, and the two most natural acquirers are already inside the tent commercially (Bristol Myers Squibb, existing TCR-T collaboration; Moderna, expanded Jan 2026 with a $5M milestone on the first mRNA-based TCER), with Gilead/Kite the obvious third given its cell-therapy manufacturing footprint. Comp provenance for what a de-risked late-stage cell therapy fetches: Gilead / Arcellx, ~$7.8B, Q1 2026 (anito-cel, late-stage BCMA CAR-T); secondary 2026 reads Eli Lilly / Kelonia ~$7B (Apr 2026, cell-therapy platform) and UCB / Neurona up to $1.15B (Apr 2026, clinical-stage). Against a $2.72B win-leg market cap, the Arcellx print says a positive SUPRAME plausibly clears above $20 rather than below it - but I am NOT lifting the target on that, because takeout is unconditioned optionality sitting on top of a readout that has not happened. It is upside skew for the Director to note, not a number.

VALUATION-METHOD NOTE. binary_prob confirmed as the right frame; no deck-mark gate applies (not commodity-linked).

VNDA.thesis_summary: Vanda ($5.23, 60.1M sh, $315M cap) carries a hard, forward-dated FDA binary: the imsidolimab (anti-IL-36R mAb) BLA for generalized pustular psoriasis, PDUFA target action date 2026-12-12, accepted for filing 2026-02-25. The pivotal record is clean and public — GEMINI-1 met its primary endpoint (53.3% vs 13.3% GPPPGA 0/1 at wk4, p=0.0131), published in NEJM Evidence 2026-04-28, with orphan designation in the US, EU (2026-07-16) and Japan (2026-05-27). The event is idiosyncratic (a single agency decision on its own dossier) and unfired. It sits on top of a real commercial base — 2026 revenue guided $240-290M, Fanapt +26% in Q1 — that the market currently values at roughly 0.47x sales after netting cash, so very little imsidolimab value is embedded in the tape. The offsetting fact is a balance sheet running down fast: cash+ST investments fell $61.5M in Q1-26 alone, to $202.3M, and management has guided 2026 burn above 2025's.
VNDA.kill_risk: Financing gap ahead of the event. Net cash/share has collapsed from the ~$6.75 the board itself cited in 2024 when rejecting Cycle Pharma's $8.00 cash bid, to $3.37 at 2026-03-31 — Q1-26 alone consumed $61.5M of cash+ST investments, and management guided 2026 burn above 2025. A registration statement went effective 2026-05-05 (EFFECT, CIK 1347178), i.e. the shelf is armed. An equity raise between the 2026-08-05 Q2 print and the 2026-12-12 PDUFA would dilute the win leg before it pays, and every quarter of burn erodes the downside floor by roughly $0.58/sh of net cash. Second, independent risk: imsidolimab is Vanda's FIRST biologic BLA, so CMC and pre-approval-inspection failure — the modal CRL cause and entirely invisible from the efficacy record above — is not covered by the strong GEMINI-1 result. The historical "Vanda always loses at FDA" bear case (Hetlioz jet-lag CRL 2026-01-08, tradipitant gastroparesis) is the weaker objection and I discount it: FDA approved BYSANTI on 2026-02-20 and NEREUS in 2026, two on-time wins this year.

The scan appears to have grabbed the next calendar event and mislabeled it as the approval decision. ALVO.thesis_summary: Alvotech resubmitted US BLAs for AVT05 (Simponi/Simponi Aria biosimilar) and AVT06 (Eylea 2mg biosimilar) on 2026-06-04 after the Jan-2026 facility-driven CRLs; the company states it "expects the FDA to conduct a six-month review," clocking an approval decision to roughly 2026-12-04. The defect that caused the CRLs was site-specific (deficiencies from the July-2025 Reykjavik pre-license inspection), and on 2026-07-29 the FDA closed its May-2026 re-inspection of that same facility as Voluntary Action Indicated (VAI) - i.e. no OAI, no approval-withholding classification. That is the single gating condition being cleared while the review clock runs, and it post-dates the board's 2026-06-08 valuation. Teva commercializes both assets. The equity is a thin stub over ~$1.53B debt and negative book equity (-$282M), so the December decision is genuinely binary at the equity level.
ALVO.kill_risk: The Q2 print on 2026-08-19 can spend the position before the catalyst ever resolves. Consensus Q2 revenue is $103M; with Q1 at $105.9M, H1 lands near $209M against unchanged FY guidance of $650-700M, requiring $441-491M in H2 - a 2.1-2.3x step-up off the H1 run-rate. A guidance cut re-rates the stub on leverage and cash burn, not on FDA odds, and there is precedent: the Jan-2026 CRL was accompanied by a slashed revenue guide and a 58% cut to adjusted EBITDA. The financing pattern corroborates stress rather than strength - $165M of equity issued at $3.75 (closed 06-17) followed by a $75M GoldenTree term loan just two weeks later (07-01). Separately, Celtic Lux (the founder vehicle) pledged 88,940,619 shares plus 7,007,321 depository receipts on 2026-06-26, ten days after buying 10.13M shares at $3.75; a pledged ~28% of the share count against a stock already near its 52-week low is a forced-sale vector that can break the $2.40 floor for reasons unrelated to the BLAs. Also note the December date is derived, not FDA-published (see dossier_note).

ARITHMETIC. The board's set reproduces exactly at the live price, so the errors are inputs, not math: win 6.00 / lose 2.75 / p 0.65 from 3.79 gives up +58.3%, down -27.4%, R:R 2.12, EV +28.3% - byte-matching the board's payoff 2.12 and ev_pct 0.283. TAKEOUT LENS - NO LIFT APPLIED, and I want that on the record. ALVO is bio/pharma by label but does not fit the 2026 takeout regime, which is bidding clean late-stage/commercially-ready ASSETS. SKEPTIC PASS. Load-bearing claim tested: "VAI clears the path, so the December decision approves." Strongest refutation I can mount from the live record - VAI is not an approval commitment. The FDA still issued a Form 483 at the close of the May-2026 inspection, and VAI explicitly means objectionable conditions were FOUND but did not warrant regulatory action; it removes the site as a blocker without speaking to product-specific review issues in either BLA. Sequencing is favourable (resubmitted 06-04, inspection closed 07-29, decision ~Dec) but the company has now missed on this exact axis once, and Hagens Berman is investigating the adequacy of its manufacturing and regulatory-status disclosures. IFF.thesis_summary: IFF has signed away its two lowest-multiple businesses and is now a dated deleveraging/SoP story rather than a vague "portfolio optimization" watch item. The load-bearing event is the definitive sale of Food Ingredients to CVC funds (signed 2026-05-29, ~$4.3B EV, ~10x EBITDA, ~$3.8B net cash to IFF plus a retained ~10% stake and board seat), guided to close by end of Q2 2027; a second signed sale of the botanical-extracts/vitamins-and-minerals/food-enhancement portfolio to SuanNutra (Carbyne Equity Partners, signed 2026-07-20, ~$170M 2025 revenue, price undisclosed) is guided to close by end-2026. Both are binding, forward-dated, unfired, and idiosyncratic — they resolve on regulatory clearance, EU information/consultation completion and buyer funding, not on the tape. RemainCo is a Taste/Scent/Health-&-Biosciences pure-play at ~$7.4B sales and ~$1.75B adjusted operating EBITDA, and the trade is the re-rate of that residual toward flavor-house peer multiples once ~$3.8B of proceeds retires roughly two-thirds of the $5.26B net debt stack. The entire edge is multiple expansion on the residual, not the proceeds themselves.
IFF.kill_risk: The re-rate is assumed, not contracted — and the tape has already voted against it once. At the current consolidated EV of ~$25.8B on ~$2.2B FY26E adjusted operating EBITDA, IFF trades at ~11.7x. Run the identical SoP arithmetic at IFF's OWN prevailing multiple rather than a peer multiple: $1.75B x 11.7x = $20.5B + $4.0B deal value - $5.26B net debt = $19.2B / 256M = ~$75/share, which is BELOW the $80.58 live price. Every dollar of the $91 target comes from the residual multiple travelling 11.7x -> 14x; none of it comes from the transaction, which sells $430M of EBITDA at 10x and shrinks RemainCo EBITDA by ~20%. The live record refutes the easy version of the claim: IFF fell from $78.03 (May 28) to $76.05 on announcement day and to $72.60 within seven sessions — the market priced the CVC deal as value transferred out, not value surfaced. Secondary vectors: an 11-month runway with EU works-council consultation and multi-jurisdiction clearances is a live slip risk on a PE-funded $4.3B LBO; the retained ~10% stake keeps residual exposure to the divested asset; and the entry is 12% above the 200-day and within 5% of the 52-week high, so the cheap-entry half of the setup is already gone.

IFF.dossier_note:
ARITHMETIC (all from the live record, not reproducible from the board dossier, which carried nulls in every numeric field).

Inputs. Price $80.58 (2026-08-03 close); market cap $20.572B; 256M diluted shares (FY25 10-K weighted average). Net debt $5.255B at 2026-03-31 (total debt $5.817B less $562M cash). Current EV ~$25.83B. FY25 revenue $10.89B; Q1-26 sales $2.7B with adjusted operating EBITDA $568M at 20.7% margin, so FY26E adjusted operating EBITDA ~$2.2B. NOTE the FMP GAAP EBITDA line for FY25 reads $779M — that is impairment-polluted and must not be used; the adjusted operating EBITDA figure is the company's own reported metric and the one the deal multiples are struck against.

Segment carve-out. Food Ingredients: ~$3.1B 2025 sales, ~$430M EBITDA, sold at ~$4.3B EV = ~10.0x (confirms the 10x the release cites). SuanNutra portfolio: ~$170M 2025 revenue, ~600 employees, five plants, price undisclosed — I assign ~$25M EBITDA and do not credit any proceeds, since none were disclosed. RemainCo therefore ~$7.4B sales ($10.89B - $3.1B - $0.17B) and ~$1.75B adjusted operating EBITDA ($2.2B - $0.43B - $0.025B).

FAIR VALUE ($91). RemainCo $1.75B x 14x = $24.50B. Deal value to IFF = $3.8B net cash + $0.2B retained 10% stake = $4.00B (the ~$0.3B gap to the $4.3B headline EV is taxes and fees, per the release's own net-proceeds figure). Less $5.26B net debt. Equity = $23.24B / 256M = $90.8, rounded to $91. Multiple justification: 14x sits between dsm-firmenich/Symrise-type marks and Givaudan's premium, and is the multiple the sell-side is implicitly underwriting — median PT $90, consensus $89.57, high $95. Sensitivity: 13x = $83.9; 15x = $97.7.

DOWNSIDE FLOOR ($70). Two anchors. (a) Market-revealed: with the CVC deal signed and public, IFF cleared at $72.60 on 2026-06-08 — that is the price the tape assigned to this exact fact pattern seven weeks ago. (b) No-deal fundamental: consolidated $2.2B EBITDA x 10x = $22.0B EV - $5.26B net debt = $16.74B / 256M = $65.4, which also brackets the low sell-side PT of $75 from below. I take $70 as the blend. The 52-week low of $59.14 is an April tape print and is not treated as the floor.

R:R FROM SPOT. Upside $91 - $80.58 = +$10.42 (+12.9%). Downside $80.58 - $70 = -$10.58 (-13.1%). Approximately 1:1 over an ~11-month hold. That is a thin event edge and the CRO should see it stated plainly rather than inferred.

GATES NOT APPLICABLE. Deck-mark gate: IFF is not a commodity-linked SoP/NAV name — no feasibility study or broker price deck underpins the target, which rests on a signed transaction multiple and peer trading multiples. Takeout lens: IFF is flavors/fragrances/H&B specialty ingredients, not bio/pharma; the 2026 biotech M&A regime is irrelevant here and no takeout optionality is credited. IFF at ~$20.6B equity plus $5.3B net debt is itself too large for a credible whole-co takeout and I make no such claim.

STATUS NUANCE. PENDING_HARD is emitted on the strength of the signed definitive agreements, but the DATE is issuer guidance to a quarter-end ("expected to close by the end of the second quarter of 2027"), subject to regulatory clearances and applicable information and/or consultation requirements — the latter is EU works-council language and is a routine multi-month gate on a European-heavy carve-out.
