XRN.thesis_summary: Chiron Real Estate (NYSE: XRN, ex-Global Medical REIT, 13.235M shares, $35.27) is mid-way through a self-directed recapitalization that converts a legacy net-lease medical-office book into a senior-housing operating (SHOP) platform. Announced 2026-05-06: $425M of Silverstone SHOP communities, a $100M delayed-draw convertible perpetual preferred led by Maewyn Capital, ~$200M of asset sales, a new debt facility, a 36% monthly dividend cut to $0.16, and withdrawal of 2026 guidance. Two legs have already fired: The Landing + The Riviera closed 2026-06-01 for $249M, and seven IRFs were recapitalized into an 85/15 JV with a US public pension fund at a $217M aggregate valuation on 2026-06-30. What remains forward is the third community, The Pinnacle North Bethesda, at ~$176M, company-guided to close October 2026 (broadened to Q4 2026 in the 06-01 release), plus the balance of the ~$200M disposition program. The equity is a sum-of-parts on depreciated real estate: management's own disclosure that the $249M of SHOP equals ~14% of the portfolio by gross real estate assets implies ~$1.78B of gross cost against $1.238B of depreciated assets and $668.6M of net debt, so roughly $540M (~$41/share) of accumulated depreciation sits between carrying value and cost. The market caps the legacy book at ~76% of gross cost; marking it at 85% and holding the two 2026 transacted assets at their own arms-length prices gets to ~$44/share. This is a NAV-discount repositioning story with a soft-dated deal close, not a hard binary event.
XRN.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim is that the legacy net-lease medical book is worth materially more than its depreciated carrying value, and the live record pushes back hard. (1) The one completed disposition was structured as an 85/15 JV RECAPITALIZATION rather than an outright sale - that is what issuers do when an outright bid will not clear their mark; the $217M is a headline gross asset valuation, and because I cannot see JV-level debt from the record, my $32.6M mark on the retained 15% (0.15 x $217M) OVERSTATES the retained equity if the JV is levered, which it almost certainly is. (2) The ~$540M of accumulated depreciation on a physician-practice MOB book is partly real economic obsolescence, not purely an accounting artifact, and 2026 MOB cap rates sit above the 2016-2022 acquisition cap rates - so gross cost is a ceiling, not a proxy for market value. At 75% of gross cost the SoP prints $34.22, i.e. the entire discount vanishes and the market is simply right. (3) The 36% dividend cut is a direct issuer signal that the legacy book's cash generation did not support the prior payout. (4) The pivot swaps contractual net-lease income for operating risk with 2026 guidance withdrawn and Q2 consensus at -$0.235 EPS; the first print carrying SHOP economics lands 2026-08-05 AMC, one day out and entirely unpriced by this dossier. (5) The Maewyn convertible perpetual preferred ranks ahead of the common AND converts, so it clips the top of any NAV re-rating. (6) I could not reconstruct a cap-rate NAV independently: FMP's REIT line mapping is internally contradictory (Q1-26 EBITDA + G&A annualizes to ~$115M of NOI, while revenue less implied property opex annualizes to ~$56M - a 2x spread), and the SEC 10-Q and Q1 8-K exhibits returned HTTP 403, so the SoP rests on the company's own 14%/25% portfolio-mix statistic rather than on verified NOI.

CATALYST. Real, idiosyncratic, partly spent, and only soft-dated. The board's forced-seller framing does not survive the live record (see discrepancies). Program announced 2026-05-06 alongside Q1 results: acquire three Silverstone senior-housing communities for $425M aggregate; fund with a $100M delayed-draw convertible perpetual preferred led by Maewyn Capital Partners, ~$200M of asset sales, a new debt facility, and a 36% cut in the monthly dividend to $0.16; 2026 guidance withdrawn. FIRED legs: The Landing + The Riviera (292 homes - 169 IL / 89 AL / 34 memory care, Washington DC MSA) closed 2026-06-01 for $249M, funded with cash on hand, revolver capacity and the Maewyn investment; seven inpatient rehabilitation facilities were recapitalized into a JV with a US public pension fund at a $217M aggregate valuation on 2026-06-30, the investor taking 85% of the equity. UNFIRED leg: The Pinnacle North Bethesda, MD, ~$176M under definitive purchase agreement, guided to October 2026 on 2026-05-06 and restated as Q4 2026 on 2026-06-01. Nearer information event, NOT named as the milestone because it is one day out and unpriced by this dossier: Q2 2026 results 2026-08-05 after close, call 2026-08-06 09:00 ET (company release 2026-07-16), consensus -$0.235 EPS on $37.64M revenue - the first print carrying SHOP economics and the IRF deconsolidation, and the plausible venue for guidance reinstatement.

VALUATION - SoP, arithmetic. All axes are mine; the board emitted nulls. Anchor is the company's own portfolio-mix disclosure in the 2026-06-01 release: the $249M of closed SHOP equals ~14% of the portfolio by gross real estate assets, so gross real estate cost = 249 / 0.14 = $1,778.6M. Cross-check against the same release's pro forma statement that Pinnacle plus ~$200M of sales takes SHOP to ~25%: (249 + 176) / (1,778.6 + 176 - 200) = 425 / 1,754.6 = 24.2%. Consistent, so the $1.78B gross figure is reliable. Against $1,238.0M of depreciated total assets at 2026-03-31, that implies ~$540M (~$41/share) of accumulated depreciation between carrying value and cost - the NAV wedge.

Components, pro forma post-06-30: (a) SHOP Landing + Riviera at their own 2026-06-01 arms-length price, $249M; (b) retained 15% of the IRF JV at the pension fund's own 2026-06-30 mark, 0.15 x 217 = $32.6M; (c) legacy net-lease medical book at gross cost 1,778.6 - 249 - 217 = $1,313M, marked at 85% of cost = $1,116M to reflect 2026 MOB cap rates sitting above the 2016-2022 acquisition cap rates. GAV = 249 + 32.6 + 1,116 = $1,397.2M. Less net debt $668.6M, preferred at carrying $124.1M, minority interest $20.4M = $584.1M common equity / 13.235M shares = $44.13, taken as fair_value_target $44.00 (+24.8% vs $35.27). Net debt is held at the 2026-03-31 figure because the pro forma legs roughly offset ($249M out for SHOP against ~$184M gross in from the 85% JV sale) and the JV-level debt is not visible in the record.

Sensitivity on the only free variable, the legacy mark: 90% of cost = $49.09/share; 85% = $44.13; 75% = $34.22. At 75% the discount disappears entirely - the market's current $35.27 is capitalizing the legacy book at ~76% of gross cost. That single assumption carries the whole thesis, which is why it is the kill_risk.

downside_floor $28.42 = depreciated common book value per share at 2026-03-31: ($500.211M total stockholders' equity - $124.106M preferred) / 13.235M shares, equivalent to marking the legacy book at ~67% of gross cost. It is an audited number, and a REIT mid-pivot with withdrawn guidance and a freshly cut dividend is exactly the profile that trades to and through book. -19.4% vs spot. R:R at these axes is roughly 1.3:1 - thin for an event sleeve.

No win_prob emitted: this is a NAV-discount SoP, not a binary. No takeout lens applied - REIT, not bio/pharma. No deck-mark gate - no commodity linkage; the SoP rests on two 2026 arms-length property transactions plus a cost-basis haircut, not on a price deck.

CONSTRAINTS ON THIS WORK. The SEC 10-Q (2026-05-07) and the Q1 8-K exhibit both returned HTTP 403, so I could not read portfolio NOI, cap rates, the JV debt stack, or the Maewyn conversion price directly. FMP's REIT line mapping is self-contradictory - Q1-26 EBITDA $23.714M plus G&A $5.089M annualizes to ~$115M of NOI, while revenue $38.064M less implied property opex ($38.904M cost of revenue - $14.827M D&A = $24.08M) annualizes to only ~$56M. A 2x spread makes a cap-rate NAV indefensible, which is why the SoP is built on transacted marks and the company's own gross-asset mix statistic instead. Treat the legacy-book mark as a judgement, not a measurement.

NAMS.thesis_summary: NAMS is a binary on PREVAIL, the >9,500-patient obicetrapib cardiovascular-outcomes trial, whose interim analysis is planned for 4Q2026 with the result guided to 1Q2027. Everything else - the positive 2026-07-24 CHMP opinion and the European Commission decision that follows on the standard ~67-day clock in late 2026 - is real, forward and idiosyncratic but near-automatic post-CHMP and largely priced. The board's "2026-08-05 FDA approval decision" does not exist: that date is NAMS's Q2-2026 earnings report plus an Investor Day, and no NDA is on file with FDA. Win leg holds at $60 (just above the $58 street high, unadjusted); the lose leg is a CETP-class CVOT failure worth roughly net cash plus a partnered EU royalty stream, ~$9, not the board's $14.
NAMS.kill_risk: The load-bearing claim is that the 1Q2027 PREVAIL interim result resolves this binary. The live record refutes that as the MODAL path: the interim is an efficacy-stopping look, and NewAmsterdam itself states that if PREVAIL does not stop for efficacy the trial continues to completion at end-2027. Management additionally flagged a LOWER-than-anticipated MACE rate from year one to year two - fewer accrued events means less power at the interim and a stopping boundary that is harder to clear. So the single most likely 1Q27 outcome is "trial continues": it resolves nothing, prints as a disappointment, and pushes true resolution out ~9-12 months while the sleeve carries the position. Secondary residual: Menarini holds European commercial rights, so even the win leg captures EU value only as royalties/milestones, and the $60 assumes NAMS retains and can monetize US/RoW economics it has never commercialized.

TAKEOUT LENS (undated optionality, NOT a milestone, NOT used to lift the win leg). NAMS fits the 2026 M&A profile: pivotal data in hand (BROADWAY/BROOKLYN/TANDEM), EU authorization days away, oral cardiometabolic asset with a very large TAM. Plausible acquirers: Novartis (built a CV franchise around Lp(a)/thrombosis; bought Anthos Therapeutics for up to $3.1B, announced 2025-02-13, for a late-stage CV asset) and AstraZeneca (cardiorenal-metabolic). Scale comp for a commercially-ready asset: Merck/Verona Pharma, announced 2025-07-09, ~$10B for a newly approved product. Two real dampeners: (i) Menarini already holds European commercialization, so a buyer bids for a partially encumbered asset; (ii) no rational acquirer pays the CVOT-success price BEFORE PREVAIL reads out, so takeout optionality sits behind the same gate as the thesis rather than diversifying it. Hence no uplift to $60.

The market is marking the PREVAIL binary down, not up; the market-implied win probability here is cheap relative to the sector, not rich.

PVLA.thesis_summary: Palvella Therapeutics (Wayne PA, 14.34M shares, $2.02B cap) has one asset that matters: QTORIN 3.9% rapamycin anhydrous gel for microcystic lymphatic malformations (mLM), a rare vascular malformation with ~30,000 diagnosed US patients and ZERO FDA-approved therapies. The pivotal event already fired: Phase 3 SELVA read out positive 2026-02-24 (n=49 ITT, mean +2.13 on the mLM-IGA at Week 24, p<0.001; key secondary and all four additional secondaries also p<0.001), and the stock is up ~620% off the $36 low. What is STILL unfired is the regulatory conversion: FDA granted rolling review 2026-06-22, Palvella submitted the first NDA module 2026-06-29, and guides to COMPLETING the 505(b)(2) NDA in 2H 2026 with potential US approval and launch in 1H 2027. Breakthrough Therapy and Fast Track are in hand; $261.9M cash at 3/31/26 after the upsized $230M February raise fully funds submission, launch build-out, and the 2H26 Phase 3 start in cutaneous venous malformations (75,000 US patients) plus the Phase 2 LOTU angiokeratoma readout (2H 2027). The remaining edge is therefore regulatory/commercial conversion of an already-de-risked efficacy package, not a data event - and the milestone is a guided half-year window, not a binding date.
PVLA.kill_risk: SELVA is a SINGLE-ARM, BASELINE-CONTROLLED Phase 3 whose primary endpoint is an unblinded clinician-rated global assessment (mLM-IGA). There is no vehicle arm, so neither placebo/attention effect nor natural fluctuation of a chronic lesional disease is quantified, and the assessor was not blinded to treatment. That is exactly the package FDA can meet with a CRL demanding a controlled confirmatory trial - which would reset the timeline 2-3 years and take the equity to roughly the downside floor. Compounding it: the 2043-protected IP and $100-200k/yr pricing frame collide with compounded topical sirolimus, already used off-label at vascular-anomaly centers, so payer step-edits could cap real uptake well below the ">$1B US peak" bull frame even on approval. Secondary residual: the near-term event is only NDA COMPLETION inside an undated 2H26 window - a slip into 2027 is a de-rating (roughly the $109 200-day / pre-June levels) without any thesis break, so the position can bleed on timing alone with no falsifying news.

WIN LEG ARITHMETIC (fair_value_target $195): 30,000 diagnosed US mLM patients x 15-20% steady-state treated penetration = 4,500-6,000 patients x ~$120k net = $540-720M risk-adjusted US peak (company/street bull frame is ">$1B" at $100-200k pricing; the conservative published frame is ">$200M" - I use the middle and do NOT underwrite the $1B). At 3-4x EV/peak for a de-risked, first-in-disease orphan launch with IP into 2043: $1.6-2.9B. Add ~$0.4B partial credit for cutaneous VM (75,000 US patients, Ph3 starting 2H26, TOIVA Ph2 bleeding endpoint +2.5 pts p=0.003) and token value for angiokeratoma/QTORIN pitavastatin. Total EV $2.0-3.3B + $0.23B net cash = $2.13-3.43B equity / 14.343M sh = $149-239/sh, midpoint ~$194. Round to $195, which also sits on the 12-analyst mean PT of $197.08 (high $270, low $133).

RESULTING GEOMETRY: EV = 0.80 x 195 + 0.20 x 55 = $167 vs $140.78 spot = +18.6%. R:R = (195 - 140.78)/(140.78 - 55) = 54.22/85.78 = 0.63:1. Positive EV but sub-1 reward/risk - the 620% run has already banked most of the de-risking, which is the honest read the Director should size against.

Profile fits the 2026 regime precisely: late-stage, commercially ready, first-in-disease, US-only build, single-platform, ~$2B cap, no approved competitor. PVLA is regulatorily LATER than that comp, but its $2.02B market cap ALREADY exceeds the comp's $1.25B upfront and equals its full $2.0B biodollar value.
